evidence.observation: Public acceptance contract for JSONL replay. The suite drives JsonlStorage.create/commit/open over a temp filesystem and asserts that (a) one transaction is serialized as one JSONL line and a multi-write commit as one JSON array line (lines[1] has length 3, lines[2] is not an array), and (b) reopening replays stamped state: entries carry the commit-assigned seq/timestamp, the value at pi.branch.tip/main is re-read with the seq of its `value set` write, usage rows are scanned back, and getStats() reflects the replayed history. This is exactly the replay a lineage report must reproduce from a tiny fixture.

Defines the torn-tail / corruption contract used by the demo's second scenario: an unterminated final object or array line is discarded wholesale and the file is truncated before new writes are admitted (firstSeq continues from the last complete seq), while a complete but malformed interior/final line is rejected with a `line N` error and the file is left byte-for-byte untouched. This grounds the torn-session replay assertion in lineage-report.json.

Public acceptance contract for projecting a branch's entry path into context messages. buildSessionContext is exercised over ordered parent-linked entries, proving branch order is preserved and that custom entries are only materialized through registered projectors.

evidence.symbol: it("filters non-context assistant response entries while preserving valid messages", ...)
evidence.observation: Proves the context projection drops assistant entries whose stopReason is error/aborted/deferred while keeping user, stop and toolUse messages. The demo relies on this to show that the branch tip entry (an errored assistant message) is part of the lineage but is filtered from the replayed context.

evidence.symbol: it("projects branch summaries in branch order", ...)
evidence.observation: Proves a branch_summary entry projects to a {role:'branchSummary', summary, fromId, timestamp} message in parent-chain order. This is the projection the lineage report applies when converting the tip-to-root parent relation into replay context, tying parentId ancestry to emitted context.

claims.claim: The JSONL session headers and per-line transactions are replayed in file order with one transaction per line (object for a single write, array for several), which yields the session id from the header and the branch tip from the `pi.branch.tip` value write; the two required tests assert both the single-line/array framing and the stamped-entry/value/usage replay after reopen.

A torn (unterminated) final transaction line is discarded and the file truncated before further writes, so a fixture whose last line is torn replays only complete entries and keeps the branch tip at the last fully committed `pi.branch.tip` write; complete-but-malformed lines are instead rejected without rewriting.

Parent relation is recovered by walking `parentId` from the branch tip back to the null root, and replay context is produced in that root-to-tip (branch) order, filtering assistant entries whose stopReason is error/aborted/deferred and projecting branch_summary entries as branchSummary messages.

Operating the replay + context projection on the supplied tiny fixture `ses_tiny_lineage_04` yields branch tip `e3` (seq 7), parent relation `e1 -> e2 -> e3`, three replayed entries at seqs 1/3/6, nextSeq 8, and two context messages because the tip entry e3 (stopReason error) is filtered out.

conclusion: Operated the JSONL/session replay and context-projection utilities on a supplied tiny fixture and produced a lineage report. `ses_tiny_lineage_04` has branch tip `e3` (value write seq 7), a parent relation `e1 (root, null) -> e2 -> e3`, and replays to three stamped entries (seqs 1, 3, 6) with nextSeq 8 and replayed values `pi.branch.tip/main = e3` and `pi.session.name = "tiny-lineage"`. The replayed context contains the user root and the accepted `stop` assistant message; the errored tip entry e3 is present in the lineage but filtered from context by the projection contract. A torn-tail variant replays three complete entries, discards the unterminated `e4-torn` record, and keeps the branch tip at `e2`, matching the truncate-before-writes contract. Because the workspace has no `node_modules`, the TypeScript acceptance suites themselves could not be executed; the demo reimplements the same documented algorithm with Node built-ins and self-checks its output.

validation.notes: Exit code 0 with `lineage self-check: OK (11 assertions)`; the run also wrote .prale-eval/lineage-report.json and the fixtures .prale-eval/fixtures/tiny-session.jsonl and .prale-eval/fixtures/tiny-session-torn.jsonl. The focused upstream acceptance suites (`packages/agent/test/harness/jsonl-storage.test.ts` and `packages/agent/test/harness/session-context.test.ts`, normally run via `npm --prefix packages/agent run test:harness`) could NOT be executed: this sandbox has no installed workspace dependencies (`node_modules` and `packages/agent/node_modules` are absent, and vitest/tsx/`@earendil-works/pi-ai` are unavailable), and dependencies must not be installed. The self-contained demo therefore reproduces the same replay/projection algorithm using only Node built-ins and asserts the expected lineage values; this limitation is recorded here rather than hidden.
